message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with detailed information about the bones of the head (skull).

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are divided into two main groups:

1. **Cranial bones (Neurocranium)** - 8 bones that form the protective case around the brain
2. **Facial bones (Viscerocranium)** - 14 bones that form the structure of the face

---

## Cranial Bones (8 bones)

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** | Forms the forehead and upper part of the eye sockets |
| **Parietal bones (2)** | Form the roof and upper sides of the cranium |
| **Temporal bones (2)** | Located on the sides of the skull; contain structures for hearing and balance |
| **Occipital bone** | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the foramen magnum |
| **Sphenoid bone** | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base of the skull; articulates with almost all other cranial bones |
| **Ethmoid bone** | Located between the eyes; forms part of the nasal cavity and eye sockets |

---

## Facial Bones (14 bones)

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** | Lower jaw; the **only movable bone** in the skull |
| **Maxillae (2)** | Upper jaw; hold the upper teeth |
| **Zygomatic bones (2)** | Cheekbones |
| **Nasal bones (2)** | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones (2)** | Small bones in the inner corner of the eye sockets |
| **Palatine bones (2)** | Form the back part of the hard palate |
| **Vomer** | Forms part of the nasal septum |
| **Inferior nasal conchae (2)** | Scroll-like bones in the nasal cavity |

---

## Key Features and Functions

- **Sutures**: Fibrous joints that connect most skull bones (e.g., coronal, sagittal, and lambdoid sutures)
- **Foramina**: Openings in the skull for nerves and blood vessels to pass through
- **Protection**: The skull protects the brain, sensory organs (eyes, ears), and other vital structures
- **Support**: Provides attachment points for muscles involved in chewing, facial expression, and head movement

---

## The Only Movable Bone

The **mandible (lower jaw)** is the only movable bone in the skull. It articulates with the temporal bone at the **temporomandibular joint (TMJ)**, enabling chewing, speaking, and other jaw movements.

---

## Additional Bones (when counting 29)

- **Hyoid bone** - Located in the neck, supports the tongue
- **Auditory ossicles (6)** - Three tiny bones in each middle ear (malleus, incus, stapes)

---

1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull

3. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
4. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
5. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
